claim: A loaded 5,000-tonne goods train at 75 km/h needs more than 900 m to stop [OUR CALCULATION, illustrative] (on-screen 5,000 T · 75 KM/H; ≈ 930 M · ILLUSTRATIVE)
source_quote: kilometer per hour (km/h) meter per second (m/s) 2.777 778 E-01
note: Re-run: v = 75/3.6 = 20.83 m/s; 10 s equivalent brake delay = 208 m; v²/2a with a = 0.30 m/s² = 723 m; total 932 m. The 0.30 m/s² and 10 s are assumptions (VO says 'fair guesses', screen says ILLUSTRATIVE): fair. v² method: https://railwaynews.net/wiki/train-braking-distance-how-long-does-a-train-take-to-stop : "Because speed is squared, doubling a train’s speed does not double its braking distance — it quadruples it." Real loaded-freight stops can be longer, so 'more than nine hundred metres' is a floor, not a maximum.

claim: On a 1-in-100 falling grade the same maths gives almost 1,300 m [OUR CALCULATION] (on-screen 1 IN 100 DOWN · ≈ 1,280 M)

(The same page's '1% downgrade adds roughly 10%' is for brisk passenger braking; at 0.30 m/s² the effect is larger, as computed.)

note: Track-side figure includes station equipment. Earlier estimate Rs 70 lakh/loco (Lok Sabha, Aug 2024).

claim: ₹50 lakh per km for about 69,000 km comes to nearly ₹35,000 crore [OUR CALCULATION] (on-screen ≈ ₹34,700 CR)
source_quote: The cost for provision of Track Side including Station equipment of Kavach is approximately Rs. 50 Lakhs/Km
note: Re-run: 69,439 × 0.5 crore = 34,719.5 crore. Gross scenario, correctly called rough maths and not an official bill.

source_quote: cost for provision of Kavach equipment on locomotives is approximately Rs. 80 Lakh/Loco.

claim: It is not only about buying boxes; they must all be made to work together
source_quote: She said the production of the safety system has to be ramped up by the suppliers for ensuring faster implementation of the Kavach project across the country's railway network.
note: Other view: the Railway Board chair (PTI, 17 Jun 2024) named supplier production as a limit, and PIB (19 Mar 2025) says 'To increase capacity and scale of implementation, trials and approval of more OEMs are at different stages.' Integration work is real (next rows), but ranking it 'the hardest part' is our opinion. Soften (see fact-check.md).

claim: Every station's signalling data must be entered and checked, and every type of engine must be wired to its own brakes
source_quote: Using this information, along with train position, speed, and track profile (such as gradients and speed limits), the wayside system calculates the Movement Authority
note: RDSO publishes a 'Factory Acceptance Test (FAT) Procedure for Stationary KAVACH Application Logic' (SIF 0515 v1.2, 27 Jan 2025) and a committee report (RM 197) noting the brake interface must talk to different loco brake systems (E70 or CCB): titles and summaries seen in the search index; RDSO host blocked here. Onboard brake link: https://www.ieiup.org.in/events/railwaykawach/Development_Kavach_System_for_Railways.pdf : "Break Interface Unit"; separate tenders for 6,300 electric and 2,679 diesel locos (PIB 13 Feb 2026). Keep cite [RDSO | FAT SCHEME 2025] only if the owner opens it; else [PIB | FEB 2026].

claim: Radio must cover every curve and yard, then everything is tested together, fixed and tested again before a kilometre is called working (on-screen COMMISSIONED)
source_quote: After extensive and elaborate trials in 324 kms of Mathura-Kota section for advance version of Kavach 4.0, this section is approved by Independent Safety Assessor (ISA).
note: Towers: 'Installation of telecom Towers throughout the section' (PIB 05 Aug 2026). Cite [RDSO | TYPE TEST 4.0] not opened here: use [RAJYA SABHA | AUG 2025].

claim: For years three Indian companies supplied Kavach: Medha, HBL and Kernex (on-screen MEDHA · HBL · KERNEX)
source_quote: Kavach was developed by the Research Design and Standards Organisation (RDSO) under Indian Railways in collaboration with three Indian vendors — Medha Servo Drives Pvt Ltd, HBL Power Systems Ltd and Kernex Microsystems.
note: Also IEI (28 Sep 2024): https://www.ieiup.org.in/events/railwaykawach/Development_Kavach_System_for_Railways.pdf : "Approved Source: Medha Servo, HBL Power System and Kernex"; Business Today (19 Feb 2024); PIB (19 Mar 2025): 'Currently, 3 OEMs are approved for supply of Kavach System.' Cite [SCR | KAVACH OVERVIEW] not opened (scr.indianrailways.gov.in blocked): use [PIB | MAR 2025 · IEI | SEP 2024].

claim: New companies are trying to join
source_quote: To increase capacity and scale of implementation, trials and approval of more OEMs are at different stages.
note: IEI (Sep 2024) lists 'Under Approval: G G Tronics, Quadrant Future Tek, Areca Embedded Systems, Lotus Wireless Technologies, BHEL, KYOSAN and SIEMENS'.

claim: Quadrant Future Tek told the stock exchange in May 2026 that it got permission for passenger trials; a step, not final approval (on-screen PASSENGER TRIALS ≠ FINAL APPROVAL)
source_quote: We are pleased to inform you that Quadrant Future tek has received permission from the Indian Railways (RDSO) to commence passenger trials for its Automatic Train Protection System – Kavach 4.0, that is final phase of securing the approval for commercial deployment of the technology.
note: Attributed to the company's own filing in v1.1.

claim: Case one: Bahanaga Bazar station near Balasore in Odisha, 2 June 2023 (on-screen BAHANAGA BAZAR · 2 JUN 2023)
source_quote: BAHANAGA BAZAR STATION ON 02.06.2023 AT ABOUT 18:56 HOURS
note: Odisha: Rajya Sabha USQ 270 (21 Jul 2023) https://sansad.in/getFile/annex/260/AU270.pdf?source=pqars : "regarding the triple train accident at Balasore in Odisha;".

claim: The Coromandel Express was coming in at about 128 km/h (on-screen ≈ 128 KM/H)
source_quote: the train was approaching the BNBR station at a speed of 128 kmph
note: CRS Accident III, printed p.10.

claim: The signal showed green for the main line, but the crossover (17A/B) was set to the loop line where a goods train stood (on-screen GREEN · MAIN LINE; CROSSOVER 17A/B → LOOP)
source_quote: the UP Home Signal indicated Green aspect for run-through movement on the UP main line of the station, but the crossover connecting the Up main line to the Up loop line (crossover 17A/B) was set to the UP loop line
note: Goods train N/DDIP 'standing there' (same paragraph). 'Set towards the loop' is the right wording (not 'locked').

claim: The official inquiry found lapses in signalling circuit work done at the station
source_quote: The rear-collision was due to the lapses in the signalling-circuit-alteration carried out at the North Signal Goomty (of the station) in the past, and during the execution of the signalling work related to replacement of Electric Lifting Barrier for level crossing gate no. 94 at the Station.
note: Fair paraphrase.

claim: Close to three hundred people lost their lives at Balasore
source_quote: In the unfortunate Balasore train accident on 02.06.2023, 295 passengers lost their live,
note: Rajya Sabha USQ 311, 21 Jul 2023 (spelling 'live' as in source). Some later reports say 296. 'Close to three hundred' is fair. Cite [MINISTRY OF RAILWAYS]: better [RAJYA SABHA | JUL 2023].

claim: Nobody can say for sure whether Kavach would have stopped Balasore; 'surely yes' and 'surely no' both go beyond the evidence
source_quote: Balasore train accident is not linked with the provision of Kavach.
note: Narrator's assessment. The Ministry's own position, in answer to whether Kavach would have prevented Balasore (Lok Sabha USQ 2597, 7 Aug 2024), is quoted above; the film should mention it for balance (see fact-check.md).

claim: At Balasore the signalling system itself was showing a false green
source_quote: These lapses resulted in wrong signalling to the Train No. 12841
note: CRS Accident III.

claim: Kavach acts only on the information it gets; given the same wrong information from interlocking, it could also believe the line was clear (on-screen SAME INPUT · SAME ANSWER?)
source_quote: wayside (stationary) units collect live data from station interlocking systems, including signal aspects, point positions, track occupancy, and route status.
note: Our counterfactual, correctly hedged ('could'); the premise (Kavach takes its route and point data from interlocking) is from PIB. Not a CRS finding.

claim: Kavach has extra checks of its own, like knowing from the tags which track the train is really on; no public study shows whether they would have acted in time at Balasore (on-screen UNTESTED COUNTERFACTUAL)
source_quote: If the train approaches a danger signal, exceeds permitted speed, or enters a conflicting route, Kavach automatically applies brakes
note: Track identity in tags: see K022 row. No public replay or study of a Kavach-at-Balasore case was found (searched Oct 2026). Cite [IRISET | HBL 4.0 NOTES 2026] could not be opened (iriset.railnet.gov.in blocked): use [PIB | FEB 2026].

claim: Case two: between Rangapani and Chatterhat near New Jalpaiguri in north Bengal, 17 June 2024 (on-screen RANGAPANI · 17 JUN 2024)
source_quote: REAR END COLLISION BETWEEN TRAIN NO. DN 13174 KANCHANJUNGA EXPRESS AND DN GFCJ CONTAINER BETWEEN SECTION RANGAPANI (RNI) - CHATTERHAT (CAT) BG ELECTRIFIED DOUBLE LINE SECTION OF KATIHAR DIVISION OF NORTHEAST FRONTIER RAILWAY AT 08:50 HRS. ON 17.06.2024.
note: Near New Jalpaiguri: https://ianslive.in/kanchanjunga-express-hit-by-goods-train-near-new-jalpaiguri--20240617101805 : "The Sealdah-bound Kanchanjungha Express collided with a goods train on Monday between New Jalpaiguri and Rangapani stations in West Bengal." (IANS); CM's statement placed it in Darjeeling district (north Bengal).

claim: The automatic signals on this stretch had failed (on-screen SIGNALS FAILED)
source_quote: There was failure of Automatic Block Signaling system in the RNI-CAT section sincs 5:52 Hrs.
note: Typo 'sincs' is in the source.

claim: When that happens, trains move on a paper authority at a slow and careful speed (on-screen PAPER AUTHORITY)
source_quote: trains were being given authority T/369(3b) for starter & advance starter & T/A 912 for Automatic signals.
note: Speed rule: Indian Express (16 Jul 2024) quoting the CCRS report: https://indianexpress.com/article/cities/kolkata/railway-safety-report-points-failure-automatic-signal-lapses-multiple-level-train-accident-darjeeling-9457597/ : "The loco pilot of DN 13174 (Kanchanjunga Express) followed the provision of GR 9.02 and was moving at a maximum speed or 15 kmph, stopping for one minute at the foot of the automatic signal".

claim: The inquiry found the goods train was given the wrong form, T/A 912 instead of T/D 912 (on-screen T/A 912 ≠ T/D 912)
source_quote: i. Issue of T/A 912 instead of T/D912 in case of all Signals failure violating the provision of SR9.12/1
note: The goods train 'departed RNI station at 08:44 Hrs. on Paper Authority T/369(3b) & T/A 912' (same abstract).

claim: No caution order was given, walkie-talkies were missing and training was not good enough
source_quote: ii. Non-issuing of the Caution Order as stipulated in SR9.11/1(h). iii.Non-availability of critical safety Equipment’s (Walkie-Talkie) with the loco pilot and train manager of DN GFCJ
note: Training: CRS item v 'Inadequate counseling of Loco Pilots and Station Masters about train operation in ... Automatic signaling territory creating misinterpretation and misunderstanding of Rules' ('training' is a fair plain-words paraphrase of 'counseling').

claim: The goods train reached 78 km/h and hit the Kanchanjunga Express from behind at about 40 km/h (on-screen 78 KM/H → ≈ 40 KM/H)
source_quote: At about 08:50 Hrs., train no. DN GFCJ was traveling at a speed of 78 Kmph on DN line between RNI-CAT section.
note: Same paragraph: 'rear end collision with Train no. DN 13174 Kanchanjunga Express at km 10/30 at a speed of approximately 40 kmph.'

claim: There was no working Kavach on that section (on-screen NO KAVACH HERE)
source_quote: The Railways’ ‘Kavach’ or anti-train collision system was not in place along the Guwahati-Delhi route, where a goods train collided with the Sealdah Kanchanjunga Express in the rear on Monday, a top official said.
note: PTI, 17 Jun 2024 (Railway Board chair: 'It is not there right now'). NFR official to IANS: https://ianslive.in/nfr-in-the-process-of-implementing-kavach-along-1699-route-kms--20240617180144 : "Kavach has not been installed yet in the section where the accident occurred." Lok Sabha (7 Aug 2024): Kavach so far only on 1,465 km in South Central Railway. CITE TAG: the CRS abstract does not state this; change to [RAILWAY BOARD | JUN 2024 · LOK SABHA | AUG 2024].

claim: Here Kavach could have made a real difference: with both trains fitted and the section working, it could have enforced the allowed movement and a slow speed past the failed signals (on-screen SIMULATION)
source_quote: This underscores the need for the implementation of the Automatic Train-protection system (KAVACH) on top priority.
note: Our counterfactual, hedged with 'could'. CRS (rec 3.3) also says new auto-signalling sections 'should consummate with the provision of Automatic Train Protection'. Functions: PIB lists 'Prevention of all types of train collisions: head-on, rear-end, and side-on.' Cite [RDSO | ANNEXURE I] not opened here: use [CRS | ABSTRACTS 2024–25 · PIB | FEB 2026].

claim: Some videos say Kavach would always lock the speed at exactly 15 km/h; that fifteen is the rule loco pilots follow at failed signals (GR 9.02); Kavach enforces the limits its data and settings give it (on-screen DEPENDS ON SET-UP)
source_quote: The loco pilot of DN 13174 (Kanchanjunga Express) followed the provision of GR 9.02 and was moving at a maximum speed or 15 kmph, stopping for one minute at the foot of the automatic signal
note: v1.1 fallback wording per fact-check: the 15 km/h is the General Rules speed at failed automatic signals (CCRS via Indian Express). The last clause is a general description of ATP (acts on the data it is given; see KV-072) and makes no Kavach-specific speed claim.

claim: This was not one loco pilot's mistake: the inquiry found failures in paperwork, communication and training
source_quote: occurred due to lapses at multiple levels in managing the train operations under Automatic Signal failures.
note: Indian Express/CCRS: 'some of the loco pilots followed the 15 kmph rule, while most of the loco pilots did not follow this rule. The absence of proper authority and that too without adequate information, created misinterpretation and misunderstanding about the speed to be followed'.

claim: Balasore: the signalling information itself was wrong; Kanchanjunga: the backup rules for failed signals broke down; Kavach is strongest against the second (on-screen WRONG INPUT · BROKEN BACKUP)
source_quote: Introduction of new Auto signaling sections should consummate with the provision of Automatic Train Protection.
note: CRS's Kanchanjunga recommendations call for ATP (rec 3.3, 3.4); its Balasore recommendations (3.1-3.7) are about signalling-circuit alteration practice. 'Strongest against' is our analysis, consistent with both.

claim: Kavach is a strong extra layer that brakes when a human makes a speed or signal mistake, and it needs a fitted engine, a working section, correct signalling data and enough distance (on-screen ENGINE · TRACK · DATA · DISTANCE)
source_quote: In addition, it prevents collision between two Locomotives equipped with functional KAVACH system.
note: Summary of rows above (fitted locos, commissioned sections, interlocking data, physics).
